title: NuNet: Secure framework for Edge AI with on-chain payments

ms.promise: Our initial milestone delivers a Project Scope document that outlines the architecture, target devices, and frameworks for our edge AI solution. This document will be informed by in-depth research into critical components for our edge AI solution and an initial outreach to 2 - 3 potential ecosystem partners to understand technical alignment and collaboration potential. The scope document will specify the types of distributed devices we'll target such as Personal computers and laptops, raspberry pi, etc and how our decentralized orchestration will manage AI agent deployments. It will also specify which frameworks (ex. ollama, crewai, n8n etc) and components will be used for AI agent functionality.
ms.criteria:
Report should sufficiently describe all the aspects needed to proceed further, including
・Deployment configuration showing nodes and application components
・Partners engaged in the outreach and the insights gained
・Number of devices to be used
・Number of components and frameworks analyzed and used in the AI solution and their brief purpose
・High level overview of use of DIDs and NuActor framework for deployment

Milestone 2 delivers a successful, end-to-end deployment of OpenWebUI web interface with Ollama backend using NuNet appliance running on two edge devices - Raspberry Pi 5 and Consumer Grade GPU (NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060) device. 

A video demonstration is provided which shows:
・Entire deployment workflow
・Deployment monitoring through the NuNet appliance interface
・AI inference example by chatting with a small language model (llama3.2:1b)

This establishes NuNet as the deployment layer for agentic AI workflows by demonstrating a fully working AI inference workflow using OpenWebUI deployed via the NuNet ensemble on a NuNet-onboarded device. OpenWebUI, used as the interaction layer, supports agent-enabling capabilities such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), tool calling, and persistent context. These enable development of more complex agent behaviors within the same deployment configuration without requiring changes to the underlying NuNet orchestration or deployment workflow.

ms.promise:
Fully functional contract workflow with NTX payments within the NuNet framework. The Contract functionality will automatically generate and issue payment requests to the user. Once the user approves the transaction through their wallet, the workflow will automatically submit the NTX payment to the Cardano blockchain for settlement. This can be verified using the Cardano Explorer and receipt of NTX in the specified wallet.
This will allow parties to manually make payments using NTX on Cardano Blockchain.
ms.criteria:
Entire payment workflow functioning autonomously. This includes the user receiving a payment request in NTX and ability to pay directly via their wallet to settle the transaction. 
The transaction must successfully settle on-chain without any manual intervention beyond initial user approval. A successful transaction should be confirmed on-chain within 1–2 minutes under normal network conditions and it can be seen on the Cardano Explorer. 
The Contract must automatically update its state based on successful on-chain transaction between parties of the contract. This will be visible on the Nunet
ms.report:
Output
Milestone 3 delivers a successful modification to NuNet contract framework to support NTX payments on Cardano. Users can approve via Eternl Wallet to settle any transaction generated with respect to a deployment on NuNet network.
A video demonstration is provided which shows how payments can be made via the NuNet appliance for a deployment which is made under a specific contract. The Contract functionality automatically generates and issues payment requests to the user. 
There is a real time conversion step as compute is priced in a stable asset (USD). Upon approval in the wallet, transactions are automatically submitted to Cardano blockchain. It is very easy to verify the settlement on the Cardano explorer using the available link on the NuNet Appliance interface.
Notes:
・Contracts are the mechanism by which NuNet ensures terms and conditions are recorded and enforced between participants
・Device Management Service (DMS) is the core component of NuNet protocol. To learn more, please look at our documentation

Acceptance Criteria
